name: Deb Haaland
subject: Can I tell you a bit about my story?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | |
---
Hey, friend — it’s Deb. Can I tell you a bit about my story?

From my great-grandmother, mother, and many before them, I’m blessed to come from generations of Pueblo women who taught me what it means to be fierce and resilient.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk911-su-nd&t=1&akid=10404%2E400544%2EDV1uB-)
Some of my earliest memories are of watching my grandmother bake bread in her mud oven and stir huge pots of [**posole**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk911-su-nd&t=2&akid=10404%2E400544%2EDV1uB-). I’d perch myself outside and watch her through the window for hours. To this day, there’s nothing I enjoy more than making traditional New Mexican meals for my friends and family.
For me, cooking has always been a way to foster connection and build community, which is exactly what we’re doing now in this campaign. I’ve had the chance to sit down with New Mexicans in living rooms, at kitchen tables, in restaurants, parks — in all 33 counties — to hear about their lives, their struggles, and their hopes for the future. Those conversations are a reminder of just how high the stakes are in this race and why I’m in it: **to fight for and deliver for New Mexicans.**
Friend, more and more, we are seeing extremism take place and a President who isn’t fighting for us. Democratic Governors — including this seat right here in New Mexico — are essential to serve as a backstop when the federal government abuses its resources and undermines civil liberties.
As Governor, I will fight to expand healthcare access, lower costs, build stronger schools, and invest in safer communities. Meanwhile, the Republicans in this race want to open New Mexico to Trump’s extremist agenda. **That’s why this race is so important.**
Fox News is calling New Mexico a top flip opportunity for Republicans. Now more than ever, the support of every single member of this team matters.
I feel so grateful for this grassroots community — including you, friend. [**Since you're a member of our team, I’d like to share my favorite New Mexican recipe, green chile chicken posole, with you today.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk911-su-nd&t=3&akid=10404%2E400544%2EDV1uB-)**** This recipe means a lot to my family, and I hope that you’ll enjoy it with your family, too.
| | [VIEW RECIPE >>>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk911-su-nd&t=4&akid=10404%2E400544%2EDV1uB-)
---
Friend, thank you for letting me take a moment of your time to share my story and why this campaign means so much to me. We’ve got a lot of work ahead, so fuel up with a pot of posole and get ready! With good food and good friends, we can do anything.
Be Fierce,
Deb
|

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: I can’t stop thinking about this...
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
Peter, I know it’s late, but I can’t stop thinking about these AIPAC ads.
In case you missed it, AIPAC-aligned groups have unleashed **_$16 million_** worth of ads to try and prop up their preferred candidate.
I know. It’s a lot to wrap your head around. But can I be brutally honest with you, Peter?
**I think we can still win.**
AIPAC has done this before in primary races like this one. They've spent millions to target campaigns who wouldn’t play by their rules, and most of those races, one of these two scenarios plays out:
1. When a campaign has the resources to tell its own story, AIPAC's ads don't stick the way they're supposed to.
2. When a campaign runs dry and can't respond — that's when AIPAC’s ads seal their fate.

So the honest answer to whether we get through this isn't complicated. **It comes down to whether we have enough grassroots power to run our own ads, reach voters, and control our own narrative before AIPAC controls it for us.**
I wouldn't be writing to you if I didn't believe that what you do tonight matters to what happens in this race. Peter, if you can pitch in $5 or anything to fuel our campaign, it would make a huge impact. Can I count on your support?

body:
Dear Friend,

Rob Port has a lot to say about what we as Democrats believe. Yesterday, he
made another miscalculation
<https://www.inforum.com/opinion/columns/port-democrats-set-to-repeat-their-oil-boom-blunder>:
that Democrats are on the wrong side of the data center issue, and we were
too alarmist about the Oil Boom.

The AI Data Center land rush is not the same as the Oil Boom. One creates
energy, the other takes it away.

If you agree that data centers need more oversight, join our movement..
<https://www.thompson4nd.com/donate>

[image: image.png] <https://www.thompson4nd.com/donate>

I’ve been in the oil patch for 15 years. Data centers are not the Bakken
oil field. The Bakken was studied before industry came to town. Where have
the data center studies been? What will be the long-term impact 15 or even
50 years from now? And why in the world are public officials signing NDAs
for data center projects? If you want those same answers, join us
<https://www.thompson4nd.com/donate>.

I seem to be the only candidate talking to concerned citizens and doing
research on this. You can see my work here
<https://www.thompson4nd.com/data-center-resources>.

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

**Whatever happened to the metal lunch box?** For about 35 years, the most contested real estate in American pop culture measured roughly 8 inches by 7 inches: the side of a steel lunch box. From 1950 to 1985, whoever ruled the airwaves ruled the cafeteria, until plastic, economics, and worried parents brought the era clanging to a close. The lunch box began as strictly blue-collar gear, a plain metal container for the working man. The revolution came in 1950, when Aladdin Industries stamped [TV cowboy Hopalong Cassidy on a steel box](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQgOGnMVvQcRgTBg9d2NK1IzrsI1xq7Mh2EuXtq_YV-gL_L31fl-VCEiReP-lgW7e0RH6VwLVyXiqF75K5PA7uACj6UiUET3FBQHMCc8Ju8SThvejG240ZuW_YduMZoTd6GJrdgps8wwTE27R2ACudQROaVWvc-gEasb81MNh1AGOPrXFskPVKZpyIeVAa2EtNub0liXXnLbzTk3Pr0tEEu9d6L6r_UDgrnOngLI7iLqWm_G6LtOwfCmeXQmBXJcWicE7rjV1VOMeD9qXDAeAMTbb-_pIQpJhRabgeJOHvUv9F87T4EwAA__9etXcO), the first lunch box to bear a licensed image. Sales jumped from 50,000 units to 600,000 in a single year. Rival American Thermos fired back in 1953 with a full-color lithographed Roy Rogers box, and the arms race was on. Carrying last year's box was social suicide, which, of course, was the key to the whole business model. It was the Golden Age of illustrated metal lunch boxes. By the late 1970s, though, the steel box had a target on its back. Schoolyard legend holds that mothers' groups, alarmed by kids swinging their boxes like medieval maces, lobbied to have metal lunch boxes banned as weapons, starting, the story goes, with Florida. It was a perfect tale: the lunch box as both treasure and cudgel. It's also, apparently, a myth. No such Florida law was ever passed. The truth was duller and more decisive: plastic was simply cheaper, and by the early 1980s, the accountants had won the fight. Over 1,000,000 men already use it. - | Whatever happened to the metal lunch box? For about 35 years, the most contested real estate in American pop culture measured roughly 8 inches by 7 inches: the side of a steel lunch box. From 1950 to 1985, whoever ruled the airwaves ruled the cafeteria, until plastic, economics, and worried parents brought the era clanging to a close. The lunch box began as strictly blue-collar gear, a plain metal container for the working man. The revolution came in 1950, when Aladdin Industries stamped , the first lunch box to bear a licensed image. Sales jumped from 50,000 units to 600,000 in a single year. Rival American Thermos fired back in 1953 with a full-color lithographed Roy Rogers box, and the arms race was on. For three decades, the lunch box served as a kid's first public declaration of identity: Davy Crockett or Zorro, or the Monkees, Star Trek or . Carrying last year's box was social suicide, which, of course, was the key to the whole business model. It was the Golden Age of illustrated metal lunch boxes. By the late 1970s, though, the steel box had a target on its back. Schoolyard legend holds that mothers' groups, alarmed by kids swinging their boxes like medieval maces, lobbied to have metal lunch boxes banned as weapons, starting, the story goes, with Florida. It was a perfect tale: the lunch box as both treasure and cudgel. It's also, apparently, a myth. No such Florida law was ever passed. The truth was duller and more decisive: plastic was simply cheaper, and by the early 1980s, the accountants had won the fight. The end came in 1985 with marking the final metal lunch box produced before safety worries and economics finished the switch to plastic. Soft-sided nylon followed, and the steel pop-culture-branded lunch box retired to the collectibles market, where the very boxes Mom tossed out now fetch hundreds, sometimes thousands, at auction. Imagine growing up in a country where owning a Bible is illegal.

| | | | | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkcGOmzAQhp_G3ED2mHXCgUOVlFPTqlWl3RtyxgO4i21km0X79pWj5gF6_b_5fmlmXm_jTdvV-vm7dtTHPI0xjXmhT9SOcjh0xiUFRIolHIGDqrmqQZQ5UZneoNECK-rF6QxcdkqKauk7Op2h1RpbYfA-0b09Kymntj13ShGIyvaliisQQnAOqnkRctL8pZPCAJHRrOV6pZibSNt-Xy1qn3V6n0JEajC4au2XnLfE5BcGA4PhOI7GunsT4sxgmMlTDMnmz4JCXE2N-1aDqvOi_XsqjhwSzY58vgRDTF5fL6AYqC2GP4SP8McHxWgf8Nvt0r29cQ4gOgZqz25E7TZtZ8_k9cDx4ZY4hT1iUbYY0kaYrZ__IUfG7o7JKzlt12dN8Jl8ZvL69Qbjz1P96_dQP69Txd5sh11Xm9SJtXwu4mP__P_f-ujhbwAAAP__3SSjGg)

Dear Friend,

Imagine growing up in a country where owning a Bible is illegal.

Where the name of Jesus is not spoken in public. Where choosing to follow Christ could cost you your family, your job, or your freedom. Where a missionary can’t get a visa.

For millions of people, this is not a hypothetical. It is everyday life.

This summer, many of them are coming to the World Cup.

They are coming to cheer for their national team and experience something larger than themselves. When they arrive in cities across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, they will step into something they never experienced before — a place where someone can walk up to them, hand them a Gospel of John in their language, and tell them about Jesus without anyone stopping it.

_This moment is what we are preparing for._

IMB teams will be on the ground in Fan Zones and near stadiums throughout the tournament. Trained volunteers will be ready to have conversations, distribute resources, and connect fans with digital discipleship tools in their language that they can take home — back to countries where that kind of follow-up would otherwise be impossible.

For some of these fans, this will be the only time in their lives they are handed the gospel freely.

We cannot show up unprepared.

You can help us be ready by giving a gift today.

Here is what your gift does:

* $25 — 200 evangelism tracts placed directly into the hands of fans
* $50 — 25 soccer patches for sparking evangelistic conversations
* $100 — 100 Gospel of John booklets
* $250 — Rents an English Club outreach location where fans can hear the gospel in a welcoming space

At the Paris Olympics and the Winter Olympics, this approach worked. Thousands of spiritual conversations occurred. Tens of thousands of New Testaments were distributed. People made commitments to Christ during conversations with our teams. People interested in the gospel connected with discipleship tools that followed them home to their own countries.

The World Cup is far-reaching. The opportunity to connect with people who have never had access to hear the gospel is greater than anything we have seen at a single event.

But only if we are there, fully funded and fully prepared.

**Will you give today to ensure our teams are on the ground and ready for the World Cup?**

[Click here to give. ](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkcGOmzAQhp_G3ED2mHXCgUOVlFPTqlWl3RtyxgO4i21km0X79pWj5gF6_b_5fmlmXm_jTdvV-vm7dtTHPI0xjXmhT9SOcjh0xiUFRIolHIGDqrmqQZQ5UZneoNECK-rF6QxcdkqKauk7Op2h1RpbYfA-0b09Kymntj13ShGIyvaliisQQnAOqnkRctL8pZPCAJHRrOV6pZibSNt-Xy1qn3V6n0JEajC4au2XnLfE5BcGA4PhOI7GunsT4sxgmMlTDMnmz4JCXE2N-1aDqvOi_XsqjhwSzY58vgRDTF5fL6AYqC2GP4SP8McHxWgf8Nvt0r29cQ4gOgZqz25E7TZtZ8_k9cDx4ZY4hT1iUbYY0kaYrZ__IUfG7o7JKzlt12dN8Jl8ZvL69Qbjz1P96_dQP69Txd5sh11Xm9SJtXwu4mP__P_f-ujhbwAAAP__3SSjGg)

## Court Sides with SpaceX on Beach Closures
The Texas Supreme Court on Friday [unanimously rejected a challenge to the closing of Boca Chica Beach](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2yozAMhZ_GdGZs8V-42IYu227JCCOCNwYztgjJ298hd-4T3EbNGeno-_7dhhs677b7X1zJ8GsOw0Zn8sRMcbDhiDyifaS0o6VXwg03DpsbQEEtVS1BDxM6_x7KbDKjmjqdkdFNC6romk5lixl1C6pr67max6kDra2edNVSB4WtoLSZM9cxVYPWWhVa5VVVUF0WTdsqaBALUSqaHIeY80JML0yzf4cnxdyGNfNmYd6TKP4I6AX053nmj4R8hQL6i0ZA_1kT0F9VAnp1Dd39BDIde6SV5AdYRvpPlpNEZlp3lhzk6IN9yJHQLtL6kI5ISc4hym8x0uOx2YWuiiyaaT-d9y7VjSjVfUXnP6_y7wQ_DXwFAAD__-nZkAE) during SpaceX launches, ruling the groups that sued had no right to bring the case. SaveRGV, the Sierra Club, and the Carrizo/Comecrudo Nation of Texas sued in 2021, saying the closures violate a 2009 constitutional amendment, backed by 77% of voters, that guarantees public beach access. The justices said [the same amendment bars private suits](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSrCAQRb8GM62mQdGA4CVm89INrRbaGWpRLGFH5--3Zn5hkxvec-p83aYbhRi2-39a2ZZrSdPGZ45cCh-TSz9Hmcl957yT4yvTRltJW5gQsKuhq1FOnkJ8TbrydgY_yIqtND2CGswA1cMy61aaxS1I6Gc1I3vnAbltHUroXRXs-ww6lFKCktC0reJOK9P3gIZICQ3sQ0lHUx5c-KK8xFd68tG4tFbRPkrZs1D_BI4Cx_M8m3J9zHNzT0-B48o-kMBR6g4H0AJH1DWgMjVoeE9rmt0v1WH9foYYQ-6M0HBfKcQPo_ytzNPibwAAAP__h3V0iQ) to enforce beach access, affirming the trial court's dismissal. They sided with SpaceX and the General Land Office, which rely on [a 2013 state law](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOqzAQheGnMV2QPQMGChc3ilCK5Ba7xZZowAOx4mCEnYS8_Sp5he0_nSP9P-fuTM67efpPNzZpG0M38zN6TonXbgj3NfU0XGNcaOAt0kxzCrPrQILeSb0D1Vly_tUVmTW9tI3K2KiqBolN1cjsYmDsm3KwFpS2VHKvGYuyqkcLDWIDnDnzHpMalFISlczLElkXWNW1hIoIRSHZuhTWPF048UZx9K_w4DUfwi3z5pLSEgX-E9AKaAdaXAo-_8B8Cg8B7d55fwrhel8EtEcXU1hfOcVlE9ieePrmGAUeavwSoN9W4OG4Bw2YrcYuT-e9i7oShZxu5PznNv0t1sPAbwAAAP__RQx8_w) allowing the closures for launch safety. Marisa Perales, the lawyer for the groups, said the decision elevates SpaceX's interests over Texans' rights and leaves the public unable to enforce the guarantee. The court noted the tribe could still sue separately over claims the closures disrupt its religious practices.
## San Antonio Weighs Taxes vs. Cuts
San Antonio is weighing [its first property-tax-rate increase in 33 years](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uxCAQBOCnsTusBf8XFGmuu7QprTUsNgpnEGzufG8f5Ud5gbRfMTOat-tyRR_8sb3ijTSfLi4HPUogZsqLiR-ZVzTvpSQ0dBY88OB4-EWBGgQMQsnFog_PpautXsHOsiYtx0lBO48z1LueJ6cIQfUwG-dmiask61oHppf95LD2-isMBiWlhFZC0_ctDV07ThOoEbGtOiDrOeaGd2I6sbjwjHfKjYm3OuidOZWqfanUpVKXv40xU4qZm5i3Hxa_LpJns1MRq982KixSjokyPwXjKfxhMmEhgSHEB9lKXeqsbXr4EHwZxqqD7YY-fJfz_y67a_UZAAD__4tvg6o) to help close a budget gap of nearly $158 million. City staff want to raise the rate as high as state law allows without a public vote, which would cost the average homestead about $81 a year and bring in roughly $125 million over two years. City Manager Erik Walsh said even that won't be enough, and spending cuts are coming. If the council rejects the full increase, the city's backup plan leans on cuts, including eliminating [209 positions](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2S3CAQhJ8GZWzBsPohUOBE2Tl1qBrBrBYfCyqYPUl-epfOj-Bkgumu7vr618f8gSGGtP7EF418PPKcaK-RmKnMLr8LL-g-a93Q0VExYeKcwgwKOqk6CXr2GOI53xs_Lspb3dCo-wGUsb1VzXO0rXKt73o7mE4tix0sWN0aWFo0HpRvwniFqQ601spodWtbQ93d9MOgoEc04q7IB87lxk9iOrA-4pm_qNxcfjVxfDJvVZgfAiYB077vt8-KfIkCpotGwBSzwyhguqoETOo62gqYKib5jylLl1MNnkqVLzxCWuVW8kaFT8l4SPdmvp4u8Cl_56XKRyH68-3DU2KVeeOQU5WcpYu5klzefiWWK24CpqaMfttDjKF2vbir9YUhfiPw_w3_NcLfAAAA__-NVJiu), 132 of them currently filled. Councilman Marc Whyte, who opposes a higher rate, called it a temporary fix that wouldn't solve the long-term shortfall, while Councilman Jalen McKee-Rodriguez warned the job cuts would leave 132 families uncertain about their future. The council is set to adopt a final budget in September.

name: Molly Gray
subject: Happy Father's Day
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/MG%20LOGO%20-WEB%20%281%29.png]
Dear Peter,
I’m up early, getting ready to make Mike breakfast (got to get the bacon going!), and I wanted to send a quick, heartfelt Father’s Day note.
When I think of Father’s Day, I think of all the ways Mike shows up for me and the boys every single day. Whether it’s reading Jack his favorite Grumpy Monkey book for the umpteenth time, making time to shoot hoops in the driveway with our teenage boys, or being my constant, steady companion as I chase my dreams, he is always there for us—steady, loving, and unwavering.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/Screen%20Shot%202026-06-20%20at%202.51.51%20PM.png]
I’m also thinking of my father, now a grandfather to five kiddos under the age of seven, and all the life lessons he imparted to us that we’re now passing on to our own little ones. While I rolled my eyes as a kid every time I heard, “Many hands make light work”—knowing that meant picking up potatoes or planting strawberries on the farm—I find myself reflecting on those words often as I travel the state and consider how we take on the challenges we face here in Vermont.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/80898/images/Copy%20of%20IMG_2430.jpg]
To all the fathers across Vermont, thank you for all you do and for the love, guidance, and example you provide every day.
Happy Father’s Day!
Warmly,
Molly Gray

body:

Good morning, and Happy Father's Day!
Just a quick reminder, along with the holiday wishes — early voting for Tom Suozzi's Democratic Primary ends tonight.
**Make sure your ballot is cast today or on Tuesday, June 23****rd****.**
Tom's main opponent in this race is apathy, so it's more important than ever that everyone makes their voice heard. If you haven't voted yet, now's the time.
**Early Voting Locations**
Voters may visit any of the assigned Early Voting sites in their county, except in New York City, where voters are assigned to one early voting site.
* [Nassau](https://us.list-manage.com/SXs64Idhznz?e=2d63ff009b&c2id=396821bffb9b8c55034eaa50cfc7635a)
* [Suffolk](https://us.list-manage.com/Kd9_h3NlfrR?e=2d63ff009b&c2id=396821bffb9b8c55034eaa50cfc7635a)
* [Queens](https://us.list-manage.com/G0jvGHlxObZ?e=2d63ff009b&c2id=396821bffb9b8c55034eaa50cfc7635a)

Visit [https://voterlookup.elections.ny.gov/](https://us.list-manage.com/szUiEz6Hp4A?e=2d63ff009b&c2id=396821bffb9b8c55034eaa50cfc7635a) to find your election day polling site
Enjoy the day,
Team Suozzi

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: My dad, Curt
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
#

I wanted to take a quick moment to wish you a happy Father’s Day. This is the first Father’s Day since my dad died, so I thought I’d share a little bit with you about my dad Curt who we lost back in January.
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/3994?t=1&akid=2473%2E135344%2EZ38j-z)
There is no single person in my life who taught me more about integrity and decency than my dad. And no one who shaped me more as a person. I wrote a piece about what he taught me a few years ago, **[which you can read here](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/3994?t=2&akid=2473%2E135344%2EZ38j-z)**.
In a complicated world, my dad had four, uncomplicated loves: Family. Friends. Farm. Food. And the absolute peak of his happiness was when his four loves were together at the same time: grilling a great piece of meat for his family and friends at the farm.
One of the great lessons I take from his life is to find your three or four loves and focus on them consistently and intensely. Do that and your life will be well-lived.
I miss him deeply and will be thinking of him throughout the day. If you, like me, have lost a father, I know today can be difficult. I am thinking of you as well.
Thank you for reading,
Elissa

name: Adam Dunigan for Congress
subject: 155 years of catching up - Honoring Juneteenth
body:
Don't wait to vote. They didn't wait to fight for your right to.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/WP1fCJeMDyA?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)
| | | | | |

---
| |
Adam here,
On June 19, 1865, Union troops reached Galveston, Texas and announced that enslaved people there were free. The Emancipation Proclamation had been signed two and a half years earlier. Freedom existed on paper before it existed in fact — and the distance between those two things was filled by people who had every reason to make sure word never arrived.
That gap between the law and the lived reality is the story of Juneteenth. It's also, frankly, the story of this country's relationship with the right to vote. The 15th Amendment passed in 1870. It took another century, and the work of people who were beaten, jailed, and killed for it, before that promise was anything more than ink. The Voting Rights Act of 1965 didn't hand anyone a gift — it was wrenched into existence by people who refused to wait any longer for paper rights to become real ones.
I think about that legacy every time I think about why I'm running. I spent over a decade overseas working to protect the idea that people get to choose their own government. It would be strange, and a little hollow, to come home and not fight just as hard for that same idea here — especially for the communities who have had to fight hardest and longest to make it real.
---
| [DONATE $25 TODAY Help Me Fight to Ensure Everyone’s Voice is Heard ](https://us.list-manage.com/5AnjtULD11D?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0)
---
| |
We should celebrate this day. But any celebration should come with the somber understanding that Black Americans today are still living through the consequences of America’s past moral failings.
I don’t have their lived experience with that history; and I don’t claim to. But, I do have a platform now, and I’m going to use that platform to force reflection on our complicated past.
If we want a country we can be proud of, there is so much work to do. Not just for the day-to-day improvement of our lives and our government, but in correcting and contextualizing the inadequacies of our justice system and our schools.

****_(My campaign staff member Natalie in 2020. She was instrumental in organizing Black Lives Matter rallies in Northern Virginia. Making me proud as usual.)_

So today, on Juneteenth, I want to say thank you to the organizations who've spent years doing that work without much credit: groups like [**Black Voters Matter**](https://us.list-manage.com/uVKNwIhKFuL?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) , who've spent a decade getting people registered and to the polls in communities written off by everyone else. The [**NAACP**](https://us.list-manage.com/19PX3Jtxk8_?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) , still doing what it's done since 1909 — defending the right to vote, one case and one canvass at a time. And closer to home, [**Black Men Vote**](https://us.list-manage.com/cNw9az9pFQA?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0) , headquartered right here in Alexandria, working specifically to bring young Black men into a process that too often wasn't built with them in mind. None of them are partisan organizations and none of them asked for my endorsement. But they've earned my respect, and I think they've earned yours too.
Here's the thing about all of that history outlined above: it didn't happen because people were granted rights out of generosity. It happened because people showed up and used the rights they had, loudly and persistently, until the people in power had no choice but to recognize them.
We get a small version of that same chance right now. Early voting opened yesterday for our August 4 primary. You don't have to wait three more weeks. You can walk into your registrar's office today and vote.
I won't pretend our primary carries the same stakes as the fights I just described. But there's something real in the act itself. Every single person who shows up early, ahead of schedule, on their own time, is making a quiet statement: _this matters to me, and I'm not waiting to be told when to care._ That posture — showing up early, showing up loud, refusing to wait — is exactly the one this moment calls for, on every front.
Today, on Juneteenth, if you haven’t: **Go vote early**.
[**Tell a friend to do the same. And if you're able, chip in $25**](https://us.list-manage.com/9eXlGlydPG0?e=8c62ac7f38&c2id=fabe48e824e4f1229d0a62f6a8279ab0); not because we're short on time, but because the people doing this work, the ones I just named and the ones organizing in your own neighborhood, deserve to know they're not doing it alone.
Showing up on Juneteenth means showing up and putting in the work on the other 364 days too. And that’s what I’m trying to do.

body:
I'm endlessly grateful for my dad and for everything he has taught me.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=7317%2E582294%2Ed84zNh)
Team,
**Today is Father’s Day. I wanted to take a moment to talk about one of the most important people in my life — my dad, Arthur Pappas.**
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/221?c0=em_ms_cp_20260621_1.vJnX2S&refcode=em20260621-1&t=2&akid=7317%2E582294%2Ed84zNh)
I started working alongside my dad when I was 14 at our family's restaurant, the Puritan Backroom. One of his first lessons was that you should never ask anyone to do something that you aren't willing to do yourself.
**His compassion and selflessness taught me what it means to lead a life of service — whether it was in the kitchen at the restaurant or in the halls of Congress.**
I know families across New Hampshire are celebrating fathers and father figures who have passed down those same values through their example and the sacrifices they make every day.
I'm endlessly grateful for my own dad and for everything he has taught me.
**From my family to yours, I hope you have a happy and meaningful Father's Day.**
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/221?c0=em_ms_cp_20260621_1.vJnX2S&refcode=em20260621-1&t=3&akid=7317%2E582294%2Ed84zNh)
— Chris

subject: Happy Father’s Day!
body:
This work wouldn’t be possible without my husband, John.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
On this Father’s Day, I wanted to take a quick break from the campaign trail to talk about someone who usually stays behind the scenes, but who makes everything this campaign accomplishes possible — my husband, John.
Running for Governor of Texas is a massive, non-stop undertaking. The days are long, and I travel a lot. But through every single high and low, John has been my anchor.
I always say that I never planned to get into politics. I’m a mom who got mad when my son’s school was threatened for closure. **But when I chose to step up and fight back — first running for school board and later for the Texas House — John stood by me.**
Now, as we take on the biggest fight of our lives to defeat Greg Abbott in November, John is still my rock.
He’s the one keeping our family grounded, managing the chaotic schedule, and offering words of encouragement late at night when I’m feeling discouraged. He is an incredible father, an amazing husband, and a great team member.
The truth is, I would not be able to do this work without him.
Happy Father’s Day, John, and to all of the fathers and father figures.
— Gina Hinojosa

body:
|
#
| 🔵 Hi friend, 🔵

In this email, we’re going to ask you to make a [**$3 donation to this campaign,**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133721095/628862552/846650056?refcode=em-6.21.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYWQzZmQ0YS03MzZkLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=vzclT5qu44wKIkFtXKnHLjtfSfrgHdwrjkGULjhT8fo=) but first, we want to pull back the curtain and explain why your support is so important right now.
---
In just nine days, we’ll hit our end-of-quarter FEC fundraising deadline. After this, we’ll be required to report how much we’ve raised. These numbers will then be released to the public, where everyone – from election experts to our opponents – will be watching for the first sign of weakness.

And with **$2.5 million in GOP outside spending** already set to flood this district – finishing strong has never been more important.

name: Jon Ossoff
subject: Good morning, Peter
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jon Ossoff for Senate
body:
# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=2415%2E5691347%2EpL_3jy)

Peter,
As I travel across Georgia, more and more people of every background and belief tell me their stories and share their frustration about the chaos and corruption of the Trump administration.
_I spoke to a cotton grower here in Georgia about the skyrocketing prices of fertilizer and diesel caused by the war._
_I spoke to a woman in her early 60s who waits tables for a living. She’s fighting cancer. She told me she was going to lose her health coverage in the middle of chemotherapy because Trump refused to extend ACA tax credits._
***
And it’s not just Democrats and independents sharing these stories. *Republicans* take me aside, or they call me on the phone.
They tell me they’re afraid of where this President has taken us, and they don’t want it to go on.
They tell me they’re voting for a Democrat for the first time!
And it’s no mystery why: this is the cruelest and most arrogant group of people who have ever ascended to high office, and their cruelty and their arrogance are matched only by their incompetence.
***
**But it doesn’t have to be this way.**
Everywhere I go, across our state, people also tell me they are desperate for change and for new ideas.
_The student working through college who still needs food stamps to make rent, whose conscience can’t stand their tax dollars being used to lock up immigrant children here at home._
_The South Georgia farmer whose costs rise and earnings fall each year, whose kids have left the family farm, who’s still waiting for federal aid long after the storm._
_The young couple expecting their first child — who worry how they’ll afford a crib and a stroller, let alone a first home — whose health insurance just went up a thousand dollars per month._
***
I believe we can reform our corrupt politics. I believe we will escape this moral tailspin and recommit ourselves to the values that have made this country great.
But none of this is possible without victory this November, and the battle is already on. Georgia is the most crucial battleground state in the country, and this will be the tightest and hardest-fought U.S. Senate race this year.
[**So, Peter, I’m asking for your help. Will you donate $5 to my reelection campaign today? This is something you can do right now to make a real difference.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-jun26.Bh0QdH&refcode=em260621-1-f&utm_campaign=em260621-1-f&t=2&akid=2415%2E5691347%2EpL_3jy)

Peter,

Today, I’m thinking about my dad.

He was a farmer, and growing up, I learned lessons that have stayed with me my entire life: work hard, keep your word, and leave things better than you found them.

Farming isn't easy. It requires patience, resilience, and a willingness to put in the work day after day, even when nobody is watching. My father understood that, and watching him taught me that **real leadership isn't about seeking attention—it's about showing up and getting the job done.**

Those lessons are a big part of why I decided to run for Congress.

As the daughter of a farmer, this work is deeply personal to me. I know the challenges facing working families, rural communities, and the people who keep our economy moving. I've seen firsthand the value of hard work and the importance of having leaders who understand what everyday Americans are going through.

That's why I've focused on delivering results, standing up for Maryland families, and fighting for practical solutions—not political games or special interests.

This election is about the kind of leadership we want to send to Washington.

Will we choose leaders who understand the value of hard work, service, and community? Or will we allow money and self-interest to drown out the voices of the people who deserve to be heard?

If you believe in the kind of leadership my father taught me—leadership that rolls up its sleeves and gets to work—I hope you'll consider going out to vote “April Delaney” in this Primary.

With Gratitude,

April McClain Delaney

P.S. My father taught me that nothing worth having comes easy. That’s true on the farm and in politics. name: Ken Martin
subject: Happy Father's Day
body:
---
Hi Derek — it’s Ken Martin. I wanted to take a moment to wish a Happy Father’s Day to everybody out there who is celebrating and enjoying time with family today. I wouldn’t be who I am today without my family, and they are such a large part of what drives me to do the work that I do. We’re living in a country where it is far too hard for parents to provide their children with the lives and opportunities that they deserve. We have a president who has made it clear that he doesn’t care whether working people can afford to put a roof over their children's heads, or give them school supplies every fall, or even a meal every night. **That is why I care so much about this work.** **I’m fighting every day for a better future for not only my own children, but also for families all across the country who are sick of Trump raising costs higher and higher, ripping healthcare away from people, and making it harder to find a good job.** So today, I’m sending well wishes to every family across the country celebrating Father’s Day, and I’m inviting you all to reflect with me on the importance of fighting for a better future today and every day. Thank you, Ken Ken Martin
DNC Chair

_If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

body:
VoteVets spent extensively over the course of the last twelve months to get the right candidates on the ballot in the right places.
#
Peter,
Coming to you with a moment of complete honesty: Our tank is running low.
VoteVets spent extensively over the course of the last twelve months to get the right candidates on the ballot in the right places. We spent $12 million helping Josh Turek win the primary in Iowa’s Senate race and Rebecca Bennett in NJ-07, and the total amount across all our candidates is millions and millions of dollars higher.
That might not sound like much when you think about Elon Musk’s trillion-dollar net worth, or the billions Republicans are putting together to stop us.

body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1527%2E1086043%2EO2REEc)
Happy Father’s Day, Peter.
I don't often get to be the one writing to you, but today felt like the right moment.
Wes is many things — a Governor, veteran, and an amazing life partner. But nothing lights him up the way James and Mia do.
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260621-1.sZFjnW&refcode=em-20260621-1&t=2&akid=1527%2E1086043%2EO2REEc)
Our children are his world, and every decision Wes makes — every early morning, every late night, every mile across this state — is driven by the same thing: **making sure they, and every child in Maryland, can achieve anything they set their minds to.**
So today, on behalf of our whole family, I just want to say: thank you for sticking with us and believing in what we're building together.
With gratitude,
Dawn

| | | Stop the chaos.

Folks, this is what elected leaders must do in the face of an administration that is intent on destroying our democracy for their own gain.

I have spent my career working for North Carolinians. Advocating for more resources for students in public schools and better pay for teachers. Building a clean energy economy to bring good‐paying jobs to our communities while protecting this planet. Defending the right to cast a ballot and participate in our democracy. #### Hi Neighbor,
The campaign is really heating up. We’re getting some national attention, and people out on the trail are incredibly receptive to this independent movement. We have a real shot at winning, but I need boots on the ground as we head into the July sprint. Here are a few quick ways you can help right now:
---
| | | |
#### **Window Posters Available**
Many local businesses have already agreed to place an 11x17” poster in their windows. I am hitting the pavement this week to get more of these up along the upcoming 4th of July parade routes. If you know a business owner who might take a poster, or if you want to walk the route with me this week to hand them out, please let me know! If interested, simply reply directly to this email or [**sign up to volunteer**](https://z6h1.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=6a37f521b78de031887ce7b7&u=https%3A%2F%2Fjamesforwashington.com%2Fvolunteer%3Fss_source%3Dsscampaigns%26ss_campaign_id%3D6a37e8f9613bcb2b6e685952%26ss_email_id%3D6a37f521b78de031887ce7b7%26ss_campaign_name%3DYard%2Bsigns%2Bare%2Barriving%2521%2B%2528Plus%2Ba%2Bfew%2Bquick%2Bupdates%2529%26ss_campaign_sent_date%3D2026-06-21T14%253A29%253A13Z&w=6961c5be930d3931eefba1d2&c=b_6a37e8f9613bcb2b6e685952&l=en-US&s=7pdrwTpUxgWp85WQlv5KmJMezAg%3D).
---
#### **Yard Signs Arriving this Week!**
Yard signs are almost here! I am finalizing the list of locations for our first deployment. Please reach out if you would like to pitch in and help deliver them, or if you own property near a high-traffic road and want one for your own yard.
#### **Social Media is Growing Fast**
We had over 60,000 views across our videos in just the past week! Please continue to help spread the word by liking, sharing and commenting on our posts. Every interaction forces the algorithms to show our campaign to more voters, which is exactly how we gain traction.

Happy Father’s Day from my family to yours!
Today, we're celebrating all of the fathers and father figures in our lives, and I wanted to share a little bit about my incredible husband, David. My forever Drum Major who keeps my heart on beat, my man after God's own heart, and the best dad to our three beautiful (and wild) children.
Watching David be a father has been one of the greatest privileges of my life. Every day, David shows our children what integrity looks like through his actions. He’s the dad who shows up at every school event, is fully engaged during dinner table debates, and somehow makes each of our children feel valued and loved.
Deciding to run for Congress was a family decision, and it wasn’t easy. We are taking on a great task in uncertain and dangerous times.
But my husband doesn’t just care deeply about our kids; he cares about every kid having a fair shot. He’s the kind of man who seeks to provide for his only family and serve his entire community.
We were contemplating this calling for months. We talked about what it would mean for our family, how we would manage without my paycheck, and how we would handle the demands of a campaign.
Then one night, as we were approaching our deadline to decide, our phones lit up with news that Trump was moving to dismantle the Department of Education. Special education is deeply personal to our family, and in that moment, we knew we had our answer. We had to fight. Fight against what this administration was doing and fight for our children, our neighbors, and our country.
This campaign wouldn’t exist without David. His steadiness at work and at home with our kiddos (and puppy!) allows me the flexibility to be out knocking doors, writing speeches, meeting voters, and fighting for families across this district. But he also helps the campaign in real ways every day—from putting up signs to knocking doors. And when the days are long, he's the one reminding me why what we are doing matters.
So today, I'm grateful not only for David but for every father and father figure who leads with love, sacrifice, and service. Those are the values we're fighting for in this campaign, and I'm grateful to have you with us.
SUPPORT OUR CAMPAIGN [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cbh_email-26q2?refcode=x_260621_FathersDay_act]
With love,
Christina

clean_body: [] Happy Father’s Day from my family to yours! Today, we're celebrating all of the fathers and father figures in our lives, and I wanted to share a little bit about my incredible husband, David. My forever Drum Major who keeps my heart on beat, my man after God's own heart, and the best dad to our three beautiful (and wild) children. Watching David be a father has been one of the greatest privileges of my life. Every day, David shows our children what integrity looks like through his actions. He’s the dad who shows up at every school event, is fully engaged during dinner table debates, and somehow makes each of our children feel valued and loved. Deciding to run for Congress was a family decision, and it wasn’t easy. We are taking on a great task in uncertain and dangerous times. But my husband doesn’t just care deeply about our kids; he cares about every kid having a fair shot. He’s the kind of man who seeks to provide for his only family and serve his entire community. We were contemplating this calling for months. We talked about what it would mean for our family, how we would manage without my paycheck, and how we would handle the demands of a campaign. Then one night, as we were approaching our deadline to decide, our phones lit up with news that Trump was moving to dismantle the Department of Education. Special education is deeply personal to our family, and in that moment, we knew we had our answer. We had to fight. Fight against what this administration was doing and fight for our children, our neighbors, and our country. This campaign wouldn’t exist without David. His steadiness at work and at home with our kiddos (and puppy!) allows me the flexibility to be out knocking doors, writing speeches, meeting voters, and fighting for families across this district. But he also helps the campaign in real ways every day—from putting up signs to knocking doors. And when the days are long, he's the one reminding me why what we are doing matters. So today, I'm grateful not only for David but for every father and father figure who leads with love, sacrifice, and service. Those are the values we're fighting for in this campaign, and I'm grateful to have you with us. clean_body: I wasn’t supposed to win my Iowa State House races. I went door to door, crawling up stairs, dragging my wheelchair after me to talk to voters face-to-face. | = Peter, I’m humbled that Iowans have put their faith in me to serve as their Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate. And I’m humbled by all the amazing supporters who invested in our campaign to make it happen. But to win the primary, we risked everything and spent down to zero. That means to win this race we’re relying on grassroots donors like you to help us immediately refill our campaign coffers. = | = I’ll level with you, Peter: Even though Democrats' path to the Senate majority rolls through Iowa, we’re still underdogs in this must-win race. A big part of that is money. My Republican opponent Ashley Hinson has taken millions from corporate PACs, so she entered the General Election with over $6 million in the bank. And that’s before the shady dark money Republican Super PACs spend their $40 million warchest. But the thing is, I’m no stranger to tough fights. I wasn’t supposed to win my Iowa State House races. I went door to door, crawling up stairs, dragging my wheelchair after me to talk to voters face-to-face. That’s how I won a deep-red Trump district.Twice. If I had time in this campaign to drag myself up to every front porch in Iowa, believe me, I would. But I don’t. The only way we can win is to keep getting our message out on airwaves across Iowa. And to do that, we need money. Today. Not in a month or even two weeks. Right now. = | | | = | = | = | = | = Let’s do this. — Josh Turek | | = Paid for by United for Virginia's Future PAC United for Virginia's Future PAC P.O. as some game to win.

[ A ]A photo of Abdul, his two daughters, and one of their cats. They're

I’m thinking about the world they’re inheriting — the air they’ll breathe,
the schools they’ll learn in, and the democracy they’ll live in.

It’s never been clearer: Our current political system is failing them.

Too many politicians have cut deals with the corporations and billionaires
who rigged this system, and our kids are paying for it.

Our campaign is about the responsibility we have to each other and the
next generation. We’re refusing to accept that this is the best we can do.

On this Father's Day, I know exactly why I'm in this fight: To get money
out of politics, put more money into your pockets, pass Medicare for All,
and build the future our children deserve.

They are the proud parents of two children, Ryan, a former prosecutor, judge and U.S. Attorney, and daughter Shane, a speech therapist and registered nurse. They have a great daughter and son-in-law and are proud grandparents to eight grandchildren. Things you might not know about Dan : He joined a cattle drive in Montana, once got in the barrel as a rodeo clown at a Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo bull riding event, led a 13-piece Motown band in high school, and has a collection of authentic signatures from every U.S. President and the Texas Founders including Bowie, Crockett, and Travis. ### Lifting up rural voices

| | | _We’ve received a number of questions about what I’m going to do for the rural parts of the district, and I wanted to speak to that directly._
_Here’s my Rural Plan:_
* _In the short term, I plan to coordinate with state lawmakers to provide immediate assistance to our rural residents in Virginia._
* _Fund infrastructure to ensure that every community has access to clean, running water at home. Here in VA-01, that includes getting running water to Mathews County, Lancaster County, and more._
* _Fund infrastructure to allocate federal funds for public transit serving rural communities._
* _Fund Medicaid, SNAP, and WIC to their pre-Big Ugly Bill levels. Medicaid keeps rural hospitals and healthcare centers open; Rappahannock General Hospital in Lancaster County is no exception. Three rural healthcare centers in Southwest Virginia also announced they would close following the passage of the bill._
* _Overturn the limits on federal student loans included in the Big Ugly Bill so that healthcare providers can enter the profession and complete their education._
* _Expand internet access to enable people in rural communities to use telehealth and pursue remote work opportunities._
* _Incentivize healthcare providers to practice in rural areas._
* _Expand tax credits for solar energy._
* _Sign on to a federal data center moratorium to understand the extent of the resource strain and overall environmental impact. Further, create regulations for sustainable_ _data center design._
* _Expand farmers’ ability to farm affordably by eliminating tariffs impacting potash, and abolishing ICE, so that farm workers can work without fear of being racially profiled, kidnapped, or worse._
* _Diversify the type of crops farmers can grow by removing cannabis from the federal Controlled Substances Act.
_

_If you live in a rural area and want to see real change, speak up now. Tell us what policies your community needs to thrive. Send your thoughts to us at EKforVA@gmail.com._
_VA-01, your voice matters in this fight. Tell me what you need._

In honor of Father's Day, I wanted to tell you a little about how much Phil loves being a father — here's him with our son Sammy as a baby! [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133735860/628901669/-966204508?refcode=ea.b7d7003a-826d-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&ms=ea.b7d7003a-826d-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b6d6&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiN2Q3MDAzYS04MjZkLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=WrJGjtodCw9FMxVQdnpT592-VTUBXG6rgHeiHzY6mCU=) Phil always says that out of all the titles and roles he's had, his favorite one has been "dad" to our two kids. **It's true: Even as his career in public service has taken off, Phil has always shown up for our family.** Phil has always been a hands-on dad. He did his share of nighttime feedings, packed nearly all of the school lunches — complete with notes(!), read books every night before bed (from Goodnight Moon and Harry Potter to Dune and Dark Matter), and judged speech and debate tournaments. And, with his boundless energy, he is certainly the fun parent — Dungeons and Dragons games (... really, any games), trips to Dave and Buster's, and ski days at Copper Mountain. Phil always encouraged our kids to be their best — to advocate for themselves, to eat dessert sparingly, to back up arguments with facts, and to be kind to others above all else. Our whole family is so proud of Phil. (Even our dog, Zeke — rest assured that out of the four humans in our house, Phil is his favorite!) It has filled me with so much joy to see the people of our state get to know Phil and see him the way we do. **There's no doubt in my mind that Phil will be the kind of governor who will care for Colorado the same way he cares for our family.** **[Right now, we're in the last nine days before the gubernatorial primary. Ballots have already gone out, and that means voting has already started! Seeing a surge of support across our state and beyond will mean so much to him in these final days. He did his share of nighttime feedings, packed nearly all of the school lunches — complete with notes(!), read books every night before bed (from Goodnight Moon and Harry Potter to Dune and Dark Matter), and judged speech and debate tournaments. body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240905%2E444211%2EStxGHT)
Last week, for the first time ever, every single member of the Powered by People team came together in one place.
**We called it PxPCon 2026 — and we held it in Houston.**
Staff from every corner of Texas flew, drove, and took the bus to align on strategy, and sharpen the organizing work we're doing every day across this state.
It was the first time we've ever been able to do that, and it showed us something important: when this team is in the same room, incredible things happen.
And we went to work.
**Our team ran a session at the University of Houston-Downtown, meeting young and future voters face to face** — walking them through voter registration, answering questions, and personally committing to stay in touch with them until they cast their ballot.
We also gathered with our Houston super-volunteers — the people who show up week after week to make phone calls, send texts, and build the connections that no mailer can replicate. We got to look them in the eye and say thank you.
All of this — the staff convening, the campus organizing, the volunteer activating — is what it will take to reach our goal of mobilizing 100,000 new voters ahead of the midterms in November.
In 2024, we took a voter turnout rate for 18-29 year olds in our program from 37% to 79%.
This is the work that works.
**Every volunteer out there registering voters is proof of what's possible when Texans come together. We need you with us — donate today so we can keep organizing all across this great state.**

| | Father's Day always brings me back to memories of my dad. It has been 30 years since he passed, but not a day goes by that I don't think about the lessons he taught me and the example he set. My father was part of a generation that understood sacrifice in ways that can be difficult to imagine today. Growing up, I watched him work long hours and take pride in providing for the people he loved. He never cared about praise or recognition. He believed in showing up, doing the work, and treating people with dignity and respect. There are so many moments when I wish I could sit down and tell my dad about where my life has taken me. I wish he had met my children, seen them grow up and achieve all they have so far. When my father passed, I lost a piece of my heart. But I never lost the lessons he left behind. Those values shaped the home where my siblings and I grew up and continue to guide me today. Father's Day looks different for everyone. For some, it's a joyful celebration. For others, it's a heavy day of remembrance, reflection, or grief. Whatever today looks like for you, I hope you have a moment to honor the people who shaped your life and the values they passed down. Today, I am especially grateful for my father and the legacy he left behind. His story is part of my story, and it's a piece of El Paso's story, too. Happy Father's Day. While too many politicians in DC are focused on protecting their own jobs, placating special interests, or fighting just for the sake of fighting, I’m running to focus on Mississippians.

| | | | _**FROM THE DESK OF NEWT GINGRICH**_
---
Patriot, I have been studying American elections for over fifty years. I helped engineer the 1994 Republican Revolution that gave us our first House majority in decades. I know what a warning sign looks like. And I am writing to you today because **what is happening in Texas right now is one of the most serious warning signs I have seen in a generation**.

_Let me give you the facts._

A new poll from Texas Public Opinion Research shows Democrat James Talarico leading Ken Paxton 47 to 44 percent in the Texas Senate race. Cook Political Report downgraded the race from Likely Republican to Lean Republican. And Talarico has raised over $40 million for this race, including $27 million in a single quarter, the largest first-quarter fundraising haul ever recorded by a Senate candidate in American history.

Now let me give you the history, because this is where it gets alarming.

**The party that has Majority control almost always loses ground in midterm elections.** It happened to Franklin Roosevelt in 1938. It happened to Lyndon Johnson in 1966. It happened to Bill Clinton in 1994. It happened to Barack Obama in 2010. And frankly, it happened to us in 2018. The American electorate has a long and consistent pattern of using the midterm election to push back against the party in power, and anyone who tells you 2026 will be different is not being honest with you.

The Democrats know this history better than anyone. They are running and fully supporting James Talarico in Texas because they have looked at the historical map, seen the midterm pattern, calculated the fundraising numbers, and decided that Texas is winnable. And right now, the polling and the money say they may be correct.

Here is what makes this moment even more critical. Talarico had no runoff. He spent three months doing nothing but raising money and organizing for the general election. He started the general election campaign with a three-month head start, a 3-point lead, and a $38 million fundraising advantage.

**_I have seen what happens when Republicans ignore these early warning signs. I have also seen what happens when we take them seriously and fight back._**

In 1994 we took them seriously. We organized. We raised the money. We delivered a message that resonated with the American people. And we won.

**Ken Paxton can win this race.** President Trump has already called James Talarico the worst Texas candidate he has ever seen and pledged to campaign across the state for Ken. But presidential rallies do not close a $38 million fundraising gap. Only grassroots conservatives like you can do that.

[**I am asking you today, as someone who has spent five decades fighting for this country and this party, to make an urgent contribution to Ken Paxton's campaign. Someone is bearing their soul to be the most authentic person, and to truly see them for who they are isn’t always easy when you have so much history knowing them in another way. Amid the euphoria of the evening, I pulled Eric aside and sat him down. I don’t think he knew quite what I was going to say. I searched for the words, and let it out: _“You know my political party up to this point, but now is the time for me to vote for the people who are going to do better for my kids and grandkids.”_ Eric jerked forward and gave me a great big hug. Then his mom had to join in: _“Eric, I’ve been voting for you a lot longer.”_ Today, my son is the first openly out LGBTQ+ person ever elected to represent our state in Congress. And I couldn’t be prouder. Eric is one of the most compassionate people I’ve ever met, brimming with the belief that those who hate can be filled with love. And the change we seek can’t just be expected, but created by all of us -- inside our homes, and inside our communities. **Our families are stronger when we come together and support each other for who we are.** So again, Happy Father's Day to all of you. [**And if you're willing, I know Eric would appreciate your continued support ahead of his big deadline. body:
Help Us Build the Future of Democracy in Ohio

| | | | | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | Hello Peter,
I am excited to share some great news.
The Enoch for Congress campaign has officially joined **Democracy Summer 2026** , a national leadership development and grassroots organizing program founded by Congressman Jamie Raskin and led in partnership with Senator Andy Kim and Congressman Maxwell Frost.
This year, Democracy Summer is mobilizing nearly 2,000 Fellows and Scholars through partnerships with more than 140 Democratic campaigns across the country. These young leaders will receive hands-on training in voter outreach, community organizing, civic engagement, and campaign leadership.
I am honored that our campaign has been selected to participate.
Young people are already leading movements, organizing their communities, and shaping the future of our democracy. Democracy Summer gives them the opportunity to build practical skills, gain real-world experience, and become the next generation of organizers, advocates, and public servants.
But we cannot do this alone.
As we welcome Democracy Summer Fellows into our campaign, we need volunteers, mentors, and financial supporters to help us maximize this opportunity and build the grassroots movement necessary to win in Ohio's 8th Congressional District.

### We Need Volunteers
There is a place for everyone on Team Enoch.
We are currently recruiting volunteers for:• Voter Outreach
• Phone Banking
• Text Banking
• Door-to-Door Canvassing
• Voter Registration
• Event Support
• Data Entry and Administrative Support
• Social Media and Digital Communications
• Volunteer Coordination
Whether you can give two hours a week or twenty, your time can make a difference.
**Sign up to volunteer today:**
[ https://campaignhq.app/volunteer](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=d411fe85ad&e=c6e7dff14c)

### We Need Your Financial Support
Grassroots campaigns are powered by people, not special interests.Your contribution helps us:• Train and support Democracy Summer Fellows
• Reach voters across the district
• Purchase campaign literature and supplies
• Expand our field operation
• Organize community events and voter registration drives
• Build the infrastructure necessary to compete and winEvery contribution matters.$10 helps us print campaign materials.$25 helps us contact hundreds of voters.$50 helps support volunteer training and outreach.$100 helps fund voter engagement efforts throughout the district.
**Donate today:**
[ https://enochforcongress.com/donate-now](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=96eb087a81&e=c6e7dff14c)
Together, we can build a campaign that reflects the values of working families, strengthens our democracy, and creates opportunities for the next generation of leaders.Thank you for believing in this movement and for standing with us.
In solidarity,
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**
Democratic Candidate for U.S. Congress (OH-08)Committee to Elect Enoch
P.S. Democracy Summer is about investing in the future of our democracy. If you cannot volunteer, please consider making a contribution today to help us train young organizers and expand our grassroots movement across Ohio's 8th District.
You can also mail donations to the Committee to Elect Enoch:
P.O. Box 1362
West Chester, OH 45071

Today we celebrate Father's Day where we honor and or remember our fathers who are no longer with us. My father passed away almost 19 years ago, and my father-in- law passed away almost 26 years ago. Every Father's Day, I still remember them and miss the family Father's Days that we celebrated together.
Yesterday, I had the opportunity to see up close and place my hand above but not touch the inaugural Bible that was used by the father of our country, George Washington during his presidential inauguration in New York on April 30th, 1789. On that day George Washington became the father of our American democracy when he swore upon a Bible owned by the St. John's large Number 1 of the Masonic Order of New York.
President Washington swore to uphold the Constitution of the United States, and our Constitutional Republic was born.
This historic Bible is owned by the St. John's Lodge, Number 1, ancient York, Mason Masons, which is the lodge of the Freemasons, and this Bible is known as the George Washington Inaugural Bible.
This same Bible, has been used in the inaugurations of Warren G. Harding, Dwight D. Eisenhower, Jimmy Carter, and George H. W. Bush. has also been used in the funeral processions of Presidents:t George Washington, Abraham Lincoln, Andrew Jackson, and Zachary Taylor.
The Bible was printed in 1767 in London, England, and contains 103 steel engravings of maps and Old Testament scenes. It is a King James version bible. The Bible was presented to the St. John's Lodge by Jonathan Hampton in 1770.
The Bible was on display yesterday at the Greenwich Public Library with Free Masons constantly watching over it.
_**Although swearing upon a Bible may seem to be a formality, it is really an acknowledgment that we, as American democracy, are governed by a higher authority, and that is God Almighty.**_
It us important that people never forget that in our Declaration of Independence, we state the inalienable rights of man are life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. These rights are granted to us by our creator, not by governments. **We as a people established government to protect these rights. This is what distinguishes democracy from totalitarian dictatorships.**
In socialist, communist and fascist, governments, the higher authority is the state. People in these systems are subservient to the powers of the state. It is the highest authority.
**In our democracy, the higher authority is God.** Unfortunately, there a is a secular trend in our country to remove the God component from the equation. However, when you do that you are granting the highest authority to the state. This empowers the state to revoke the fundamental rights upon which our country was founded.
By being sworn in on a Bible President Washington set the precedent that all Presidents are subject to a higher authority. Presidents are not dictators, nor kings but instead the guardians of our Constitutional Republic.
_**Happy Fathers Day to the fathers and to the father of our American form of democracy and freedom - George Washington. We are the land of the free because of brave patriots like him and so many others.**_

Construction workers sign and photograph the beam that will be part of the ceiling of the Obama Presidential Library during the topping out ceremony in Jackson Park on June 10, 2024. (Marc C. Monaghan)
By Roger Stone and Mark Vargas

This week, the Obama Presidential Center will celebrate its long-awaited grand opening in Chicago. There will be speeches, celebrity appearances, glowing media coverage, and carefully choreographed tributes to “hope” and “change.”

The official dedication is scheduled for June 18, with public access beginning on Juneteenth. But behind the polished granite, soaring architecture, and endless self-congratulation lies a much uglier story.

Multiple Black-owned subcontractors that helped build the Obama Center are reportedly owed millions of dollars and are now fighting to keep their businesses alive. The very entrepreneurs the project promised to uplift through its diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives have instead become collateral damage in yet another elite progressive experiment.

It is a devastating irony.

[_**Today, we’re asking you to donate just $5 before midnight to reelect Mark Warner and keep us on track to hit our June fundraising goal.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133741693/628913999/-1133191615?amount=5&refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_FiveThings_260621_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNmYwNmIzZi04ODZkLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=yfmz9pMUnsA7JZ6ZPUGIyqTOn4H_ZRdfho9uCQEhquM=)

**And if you keep reading, we’ll share with you 5 things you may not have known about the senator from Virginia.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/133741694/628914000/-1133191615?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_FiveThings_260621_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNmYwNmIzZi04ODZkLWYxMTEtOGZjYi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2ZDYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=yfmz9pMUnsA7JZ6ZPUGIyqTOn4H_ZRdfho9uCQEhquM=)
1. **Mark grew up in a working-class household** – and was the first person in his family to graduate college. He remains committed to ensuring Virginia public schools provide the best education possible so every student can succeed.

2. **Before his career in public service, Mark was a successful businessman,** but it took a few tries. His first business failed within weeks. His second attempt failed within the first six months. His third venture broke through – and now he’s working in the Senate to expand access capital for small business owners and entrepreneurs.

3. **He knows how to get things done, even in a closely divided Congress.** Whether it's working across the aisle to invest $12 billion to help underserved communities access affordable capital, passing historic infrastructure legislation, or protecting our national security, Senator Warner has a long track record of delivering for Virginians and all Americans.

4. **He won't hesitate to call out President Trump and his acolytes when their actions threaten our freedoms, our safety, or our ability to afford a good life.** Right now, that means fighting back against Trump's executive order attacking mail-in voting, the reckless war of choice that is driving up prices at the pump and the grocery store, and the so-called Big Ugly Bill that's putting rural Virginia hospitals at risk. Chaos and corruption shouldn't be the new normal in Washington — and Mark refuses to look away.

5. **He’s running for reelection because this country is facing big challenges that require even bigger solutions.** Senator Warner is fighting to bring down costs for working families, expand health care access, restore America’s standing on the global stage, and prepare our economies for the changes brought on by artificial intelligence.

**But he can’t do it alone – this campaign is counting on the grassroot support from folks like you to send Mark back to the Senate, so he can continue speaking out and holding the Trump administration accountable.**

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]
